settings.finalizedWarning: Registration is finalized — changing the MacMahon groups will change everyone's points and future pairings.
settings.exportSettingsDesc: Download these settings as a JSON file — e.g. to compare pairing variants with the simulation tool — or load a previously exported file to apply it here.
settings.eloModeDesc: Ignore Swiss / MacMahon entirely and pair each round to minimise the ELO difference of every game, using a live Bayesian estimate of each player's strength that updates from the results.
settings.eloEstimateKnobsNote: How the live ELO estimate is computed.
settings.eloApplyToDesc: Who gets an estimated rating. "Unrated players only" trusts every rated player's registration rating and only estimates newcomers — the safe default. "All players" re-estimates everyone from the games played.
settings.eloUnratedPriorDesc: How an unrated newcomer is rated. "Performance rating" reads it straight off the field they played, with no prior — exactly as the FESA rating program does (an all-loss newcomer floors to 1, an all-win one is rated as if they drew their strongest opponent). "Tuned Laplace" instead anchors them to a fat-tailed prior tuned to let strong veterans climb while keeping the weak majority near the bottom.
settings.macmahonDesc: Each player starts with one point per threshold they reach — an ELO rating or a dan/kyu grade. For example, with thresholds 1200 ELO and 1700 ELO a player rated below 1200 starts at 0, from 1200 to 1699 at 1, and 1700 or above at 2; a grade threshold works the same way on a player's dan/kyu grade instead. ELO and grade thresholds are independent — a player is scored on each axis it configures. A player missing the value a threshold needs (no rating, no grade) never meets it. Leave the list empty to disable MacMahon.
settings.noThresholds: No thresholds — every player starts at 0 MacMahon points.
settings.categoriesDesc: Optional labels a player can carry (e.g. Women, U18, U14). None by default — add as many as you like. They show as checkbox columns in the Players tab, and the standings can be highlighted by category with each category's leader flagged. Categories are descriptive only: they never affect pairing or scoring.
settings.degressiveDesc: Check “stops after round” on a threshold to drop it once that round is complete, so the starting-point head start fades as the field converges. Each threshold can be given its own stopping round.
settings.airtightGroupsDesc: For the first N rounds, an extra rule (just below no-rematch, above equal-scores) avoids pairing players with a different number of MacMahon points — penalty grows with the square of the gap, like the other gap rules. Off by default.
settings.macmahonFromEloDesc: Award MacMahon starting points from a live ELO estimate rather than each player's registration rating: every ELO threshold is compared against the same Bayesian estimate used by ELO pairing, recomputed each round, so a player's starting points can rise or fall as their estimated strength moves. Grade thresholds are unaffected. Works with plain Swiss or ELO pairing. Off by default.
settings.macmahonFromEloCheckbox: Award MacMahon from the estimated ELO
settings.macmahonFromEloNeedsEloThreshold: Add at least one ELO threshold above to enable this.
settings.clubProtectionDesc: Avoid pairing players from the same club. Off by default. Club names are matched case-insensitively; players with no club set are never protected.
settings.clubProtectionCheckbox: Avoid pairing players from the same club
settings.exemptDesc: Clubs exempt from protection — their members may still be paired (e.g. the host club, whose entrants are expected to meet):
settings.noExemptions: No exemptions — every club is protected.
settings.floaterDesc: When a score group has to pair across groups, who floats? The weakest of the upper group always drops down; this chooses who the lower group sends up.
settings.floaterClassic: Classic Swiss — the strongest of the lower group floats up
settings.floaterMedian: Median Swiss — the median of the lower group floats up
settings.hybridCupDesc: Run a direct-elimination cup among the top eligible players alongside the Swiss (the French / European Championship format). Enabling this adds an eligibility column to registration; you pick the bracket size (top 8/16/32/64) when you finalize registration.
settings.hybridCupCheckbox: Hybrid tournament with a direct-elimination cup
settings.cupFormatDirectDesc: The top 8/16/32/64 eligible players are the bracket, which starts in round 1.
settings.cupFormatQualifierDesc: Half the bracket is pre-qualified and plays an ordinary Swiss game in round 1, while the next players play a qualification round among themselves; its winners complete the bracket, which then runs from round 2. This takes half as many eligible players again — 12, 24, 48 or 96 for a bracket of 8, 16, 32 or 64.
settings.longBoardsDesc: Let the referee flag individual boards as long games with double the time control: they last two rounds while the rest of the field plays two ordinary rounds, and the winner scores two points. Enabling this adds a per-board checkbox to the round view. The two players sit out the next round's pairing while their long game is in progress.
settings.longBoardsCheckbox: Allow two-round long games (double time control)
settings.handicapDesc: Controls the handicap column(s) in the pairings view. A recommended handicap (FFS Annexe 7, from the rating gap) is highlighted in the picker whenever it's shown, whichever option is chosen below. Cup games never have a handicap.
settings.handicapNone: No handicap games — hide the column
settings.handicapAllowed: Handicap games allowed — show the picker
settings.handicapSuggested: Handicap games suggested — also show a suggested-handicap column
settings.handicapWielCheckbox: "Wiel" rule: the giver always counts as the winner
settings.handicapWielDesc: When on, a handicap game always credits the giver as the winner in the standings and for pairing, whatever the actual result. When off (the default), handicap games score like any other game.
settings.absencesDesc: How a round a player does not play is scored by default.
settings.halfPointAbsencesCheckbox: Give a half point to absences by default
settings.halfPointAbsencesDesc: When on, a player marked absent scores half a point (shown as 0= in the cross-table) instead of zero. This is only the starting value: click any 0+/0=/0− in the standings to re-score that round for that player. It applies to rounds started from now on, and leaves rounds already played as they are. The odd-round bye still starts at a full point, and a no-show forfeit still scores nothing. Off by default.
settings.rankingDesc: Players are ranked by these criteria in order (the tournament number breaks anything still level), and only these columns appear on the Standings tab. Points is one of them — normally first, but you can reorder it like the rest. Each opponent-sum metric comes in a MacMahon-inclusive (M) and a wins-only (W) flavour.
settings.noTiebreaks: No tie-breaks — players level on points are ordered by tournament number.
settings.teamDesc: Pair teams rather than individuals: a match between two teams is one ordinary board per position, board 1 against board 1 and so on. Results are still entered per board.
settings.teamCheckbox: Run this as a team tournament
settings.teamLocked: Team mode and team size are fixed once registration is finalized.

serverError.invalidTeamSize: A team size of {size} isn't allowed — it must be between 2 and 9.
serverError.teamSettingsLocked: Team mode and team size can't be changed once registration is finalized.
serverError.teamIsFull: That team already has its {size} members.
serverError.playersWithoutTeam: {count} players are not in a team yet. Every player must be in one before finalizing.
serverError.membersWithoutPairingRating: MacMahon starting points need a pairing ELO for every unrated team member — {count} are still missing one.
serverError.notEnoughTeams: A team tournament needs at least 2 teams (there are {have}).
serverError.noLateRegistrationInTeamMode: A team tournament can't take late registrations: every player has to be in a team, and the rosters are frozen.
serverError.notEnoughPresentTeams: A round needs at least {needed} present teams — only {have} are present.
serverError.partialTeamAbsence: Only some of team {name}'s players are marked absent. Mark the whole team absent, or pair the round and record the forfeit on the board.
